summary: Intermittent streaming stalls and 504s for long completions; edge keepalive and header clipping suspected
description:
Issue summary:
Narrativa Labs reports intermittent streaming stalls and 504/502 proxy errors when rendering long completion streams (often >45s). Failures began after a gradual traffic increase on 2026-03-09 and coincide with spikes in request header sizes for a subset of calls that include long X-Customer-Metadata headers.

Impact:
- ~8% of generation requests for Narrative's prod workspace are failing or terminating early during 2026-03-09 to 2026-03-10 peak windows.
- Customer experiences truncated outputs or EOF in the middle of long responses; affects end-user flows (article generation) and causes retries that increase cost.
- No data plane model correctness regressions; issue appears infrastructural (timeouts/clipping).

Environment:
- Redwood hosted (api.redwood.ai), edge LB: aws-alb + nginx edge-proxy layer, region: us-east-1 (primary).
- Customer is enterprise tier with high concurrent streaming usage and custom metadata headers.
- Affected model: redwood-2-large pinned by customer.

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer):
1) Call /v1/chat/completions with streaming enabled, include a large X-Customer-Metadata header (~8KB) and session cookie.
2) Send prompts that produce long running token streams (avg 40-90s).
3) Observe stream stalls or connection close from server after ~30-60s; sometimes client sees 502 or 504.

Observations & logs:
- Edge access logs (ALB + edge-proxy) show many upstream reset/timeout statuses around 30s. Example request ids: rID-20260310-7f8a3, rID-20260310-8b2c1.
- Nginx edge error log snippets: "upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out) while reading response header from upstream" for requests with large headers.
- ALB metrics show increased 504 counts during the window; backend (serving) healthy target responses remain high for non-streaming quick requests.
- tcpdump from one suspect host captured FIN from proxy side while backend still transmitting data.
- No recent serving runtime changes in production for redwood-2-large since 2026-03-05 (see PRs).

Hypothesis:
1) Edge keepalive/idle timeout or proxy_buffer_size on the nginx layer is closing connections when header parsing or initial upstream handshake takes longer (large headers + TLS handshake overhead) and/or when continuous streaming keeps the request open without emitting headers within proxy idle window.
2) Header size or proxy_buffer limits are causing header clipping which trips a 502 on the ALB/nginx path for requests that include long auth/metadata headers.
3) Customer retried requests due to client-side timeouts causing thundering herd and temporary LB saturation, exacerbating latency/regression.

Investigation notes:
- Reproduced a similar failure in staging by sending an 8KB X-Customer-Metadata header and streaming a long completion; staging nginx returned "upstream prematurely closed connection" after ~35s.
- Increasing proxy_read_timeout and proxy_send_timeout on a staging edge replica to 120s removed immediate disconnects in the reproduce run.
- Increasing proxy_buffer_size to handle larger headers prevented header-related 502s in staging.
- ALB idle timeout was at default 60s and nginx keepalive timed at 30s in edge config. Mix of these settings can create premature closes during long-lived streaming sessions.

Workarounds applied (temporary):
- Elevated edge proxy timeouts (proxy_read_timeout, proxy_send_timeout) on a limited canary fleet in us-east-1 to 120s at 2026-03-10 22:45 UTC.
- Increased proxy_buffer_size on canary edge to accept up to 12KB headers.
- Notified Narrative to reduce header payloads as short-term mitigation and to enable client-side keep-alive/read-heartbeat where possible.

Next steps / action items:
- Validate canary results for 24 hours; if stable, roll change to all us-east edge nodes. Owner: Ethan Brooks. ETA: 2026-03-13.
- Add automated alert that correlates large header usage with increased 5xx/stream-abort rates. Owner: Infra Monitoring. ETA: 2026-03-15.
- Audit edge nginx configs for proxy_buffer and timeout defaults and update runbook with recommended settings for enterprise customers with long-lived streams. Owner: SRE Docs. ETA: 2026-03-18.
- Evaluate whether ALB idle timeout should be increased or if we should move to a TCP-level proxy for long streaming paths to avoid HTTP header re-processing. Owner: Network Eng. ETA: 2026-03-20.

Resolution notes (temporary):
- Canary adjustments removed the reproduction case for the specific header size/test vectors. Final resolution pending global rollout and monitoring validation.

2026-03-10 22:30 UTC - Ethan Brooks (SRE): 'Reproduced in staging with large X-Customer-Metadata header. Suspect nginx proxy_read_timeout + proxy_buffer_size. Spun up canary with increased timeouts and buffer.'

2026-03-11 09:12 UTC - Network Eng (K. Patel): 'Investigating ALB vs nginx interplay; ALB idle 60s default may be OK but nginx keepalive 30s seems aggressive for some streaming cases. Drafting change for canary.’

resolution: Temporary mitigation applied: increased proxy_read/send timeouts and buffer size on edge canary; awaiting staged rollout and monitoring. Permanent mitigation to be defined after audit of edge timeouts and ALB config.
